properties.displayName: FW-001 Firewall - Vertical port scan (one source, many ports on one host)
properties.description: Detects one source IP connecting to 25 or more different destination ports on a single destination host within one hour, as seen by FortiGate or Palo Alto firewalls. This is the pattern of a vertical port scan, where an attacker probes one machine to find which services are open. Denied and allowed connections are both counted, because most scan traffic is blocked.
properties.query:
let lookback = 1h;
let PortThreshold = 25;                  // distinct destination ports from one source to one host
let ExcludedSources = dynamic([]);       // approved scanners, e.g. vulnerability scanner IPs
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor in ("Fortinet", "Palo Alto Networks")
| where isnotempty(SourceIP) and isnotempty(DestinationIP) and isnotnull(DestinationPort)
| where not(Protocol in~ ("icmp", "1"))
| where SourceIP !in (ExcludedSources)
| summarize
    StartTime = min(TimeGenerated),
    EndTime = max(TimeGenerated),
    DistinctPorts = dcount(DestinationPort),
    SamplePorts = make_set(DestinationPort, 50),
    Actions = make_set(DeviceAction, 10),
    TotalEvents = count(),
    FirewallName = take_any(DeviceName)
    by SourceIP, DestinationIP, DeviceVendor
| where DistinctPorts >= PortThreshold
| extend Direction = case(
    ipv4_is_private(SourceIP) and ipv4_is_private(DestinationIP), "Internal",
    ipv4_is_private(SourceIP), "Outbound",
    ipv4_is_private(DestinationIP), "Inbound",
    "External")
| project StartTime, EndTime, SourceIP, DestinationIP, Direction, DistinctPorts, SamplePorts, Actions, TotalEvents, DeviceVendor, FirewallName

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: {{SourceIP}} probed {{DistinctPorts}} different ports on {{DestinationIP}} within one hour.

properties.displayName: FW-002 Firewall - Horizontal port scan (one source, one port across many hosts)
properties.description: Detects one source IP connecting to the same destination port on 20 or more different hosts within one hour. This is a horizontal scan (a port sweep), typically used to find every machine running a particular service, such as SMB (445), RDP (3389) or SSH (22).
properties.query:
let lookback = 1h;
let HostThreshold = 20;                  // distinct destination hosts on the same port
let ExcludedSources = dynamic([]);       // approved scanners, monitoring servers, domain controllers
let ExcludedPorts = dynamic([53, 123]);  // DNS and NTP fan out by design; adjust to your network
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor in ("Fortinet", "Palo Alto Networks")
| where isnotempty(SourceIP) and isnotempty(DestinationIP) and isnotnull(DestinationPort)
| where not(Protocol in~ ("icmp", "1"))
| where SourceIP !in (ExcludedSources) and DestinationPort !in (ExcludedPorts)
| summarize
    StartTime = min(TimeGenerated),
    EndTime = max(TimeGenerated),
    DistinctHosts = dcount(DestinationIP),
    SampleHosts = make_set(DestinationIP, 50),
    Actions = make_set(DeviceAction, 10),
    TotalEvents = count(),
    FirewallName = take_any(DeviceName)
    by SourceIP, DestinationPort, DeviceVendor
| where DistinctHosts >= HostThreshold
| extend Direction = iff(ipv4_is_private(SourceIP), "From internal host", "From external host")
| project StartTime, EndTime, SourceIP, DestinationPort, Direction, DistinctHosts, SampleHosts, Actions, TotalEvents, DeviceVendor, FirewallName

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: Horizontal port scan from {{SourceIP}} on port {{DestinationPort}}
alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: {{SourceIP}} connected to port {{DestinationPort}} on {{DistinctHosts}} different hosts within one hour.

properties.displayName: FW-003 Firewall - Slow port scan over 24 hours
properties.description: Detects a low-and-slow scan: one source IP touching 50 or more different host:port targets over 24 hours, spread across at least 6 separate hours, while never exceeding 20 targets in any single hour. Attackers scan slowly to stay under the one-hour thresholds used by FW-001 and FW-002; this rule catches what those miss.
properties.query:
let lookback = 1d;
let MinTotalTargets = 50;     // distinct host:port pairs over the whole day
let MinActiveHours = 6;       // the activity must be spread out
let MaxTargetsPerHour = 20;   // above this, the fast-scan rules (FW-001/FW-002) already fire
let ExcludedSources = dynamic([]);
let Base = materialize(
CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where DeviceVendor in ("Fortinet", "Palo Alto Networks")
    | where isnotempty(SourceIP) and isnotempty(DestinationIP) and isnotnull(DestinationPort)
    | where not(Protocol in~ ("icmp", "1"))
    | where SourceIP !in (ExcludedSources)
    | extend Target = strcat(DestinationIP, ":", tostring(DestinationPort))
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, Target, DeviceAction, DeviceVendor, DeviceName);
let HourlyProfile = Base
    | summarize TargetsThisHour = dcount(Target) by SourceIP, Hour = bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
    | summarize ActiveHours = count(), MaxTargetsInOneHour = max(TargetsThisHour) by SourceIP;
Base
| summarize
    StartTime = min(TimeGenerated),
    EndTime = max(TimeGenerated),
    TotalTargets = dcount(Target),
    DistinctHosts = dcount(DestinationIP),
    DistinctPorts = dcount(DestinationPort),
    SampleTargets = make_set(Target, 50),
    Actions = make_set(DeviceAction, 10),
    DeviceVendor = take_any(DeviceVendor),
    FirewallName = take_any(DeviceName)
    by SourceIP
| where TotalTargets >= MinTotalTargets
| join kind=inner HourlyProfile on SourceIP
| where ActiveHours >= MinActiveHours and MaxTargetsInOneHour < MaxTargetsPerHour
| project StartTime, EndTime, SourceIP, TotalTargets, DistinctHosts, DistinctPorts, ActiveHours, MaxTargetsInOneHour, SampleTargets, Actions, DeviceVendor, FirewallName

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: Slow port scan from {{SourceIP}} over 24 hours
alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: {{SourceIP}} reached {{TotalTargets}} different host:port targets spread over {{ActiveHours}} hours.

properties.displayName: FW-004 Firewall - ICMP ping sweep (host discovery)
properties.description: Detects one source IP sending ICMP traffic to 20 or more different destination hosts within one hour. A ping sweep is usually the first step of network discovery, used to find which hosts are alive before port scanning them.
properties.query:
let lookback = 1h;
let HostThreshold = 20;
let ExcludedSources = dynamic([]);   // monitoring tools (PRTG, Zabbix, Nagios, SolarWinds)
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor in ("Fortinet", "Palo Alto Networks")
| where Protocol in~ ("icmp", "1") or ApplicationProtocol =~ "icmp" or DestinationServiceName in~ ("PING", "ALL_ICMP", "icmp", "ping")
| where isnotempty(SourceIP) and isnotempty(DestinationIP)
| where SourceIP !in (ExcludedSources)
| summarize
    StartTime = min(TimeGenerated),
    EndTime = max(TimeGenerated),
    DistinctHosts = dcount(DestinationIP),
    SampleHosts = make_set(DestinationIP, 50),
    Actions = make_set(DeviceAction, 10),
    TotalEvents = count(),
    FirewallName = take_any(DeviceName)
    by SourceIP, DeviceVendor
| where DistinctHosts >= HostThreshold
| extend Direction = iff(ipv4_is_private(SourceIP), "From internal host", "From external host")
| project StartTime, EndTime, SourceIP, Direction, DistinctHosts, SampleHosts, Actions, TotalEvents, DeviceVendor, FirewallName

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: ICMP ping sweep from {{SourceIP}} to {{DistinctHosts}} hosts
alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: {{SourceIP}} sent ICMP traffic to {{DistinctHosts}} different hosts within one hour.

properties.displayName: FW-005 Firewall - Vertical port scan from a threat-intelligence IP
properties.description: Detects a vertical port scan (10 or more ports on one host within one hour) where the source IP is an active indicator in Microsoft Sentinel threat intelligence. The threshold is lower than FW-001 because the source is already known to be malicious.
properties.query:
let dt_lookBack = 1h;       // firewall data window
let ioc_lookBack = 14d;     // threat-intel window
let PortThreshold = 10;
let MaliciousIPs = ThreatIntelIndicators
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(ioc_lookBack)
    | where ObservableKey in ("ipv4-addr:value", "ipv6-addr:value", "network-traffic:src_ref.value", "network-traffic:dst_ref.value")
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by Id
    | where IsDeleted == false and (isnull(ValidUntil) or ValidUntil > now())
    | extend TI_Description = tostring(Data.description)
    | summarize arg_max(Confidence, TI_Description, Id) by TI_IP = ObservableValue
    | project TI_IP, TI_Confidence = Confidence, TI_Description, TI_IndicatorId = Id;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(dt_lookBack)
| where DeviceVendor in ("Fortinet", "Palo Alto Networks")
| where isnotempty(SourceIP) and isnotempty(DestinationIP) and isnotnull(DestinationPort)
| where not(Protocol in~ ("icmp", "1"))
| summarize
    StartTime = min(TimeGenerated),
    EndTime = max(TimeGenerated),
    DistinctPorts = dcount(DestinationPort),
    SamplePorts = make_set(DestinationPort, 50),
    Actions = make_set(DeviceAction, 10),
    TotalEvents = count(),
    FirewallName = take_any(DeviceName)
    by SourceIP, DestinationIP, DeviceVendor
| where DistinctPorts >= PortThreshold
| join kind=inner MaliciousIPs on $left.SourceIP == $right.TI_IP
| project StartTime, EndTime, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DistinctPorts, SamplePorts, Actions, TotalEvents, TI_Confidence, TI_Description, TI_IndicatorId, DeviceVendor, FirewallName

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: Threat-intel IP {{SourceIP}} probed {{DistinctPorts}} ports on {{DestinationIP}} within one hour.

properties.displayName: FW-007 FortiGate - Configuration change by administrator
properties.description: Detects configuration changes on FortiGate firewalls using FortiOS configuration log IDs (32102, 32104, 44544-44547, 32565, 32566). Each alert shows who made the change, from where (GUI or CLI, source IP), and what was changed (configuration path, object and attributes). Changes to high-risk areas such as firewall policies, admin accounts, VPN and logging settings are flagged.
properties.query:
let lookback = 15m;
// FortiOS log IDs for configuration activity (CEF carries the last 5 digits, e.g. 0100044546 -> 44546)
let ConfigLogIds = dynamic(["32102", "32104", "44544", "44545", "44546", "44547", "32565", "32566"]);
// Paths where a change deserves extra attention
let HighRiskPaths = dynamic(["firewall.policy", "system.admin", "user.local", "user.group", "vpn.", "log.", "system.interface", "router.", "system.global", "firewall.address", "system.api-user"]);
let ApprovedAdmins = dynamic([]);   // optional: change-managed service accounts to exclude
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet" and DeviceProduct startswith "Fortigate"
| extend LogId = iff(strlen(DeviceEventClassID) > 5, substring(DeviceEventClassID, strlen(DeviceEventClassID) - 5), DeviceEventClassID)
| where LogId in (ConfigLogIds)
| extend
    AdminUser = coalesce(DestinationUserName, SourceUserName, extract(@"FTNTFGTuser=([^;]+)", 1, AdditionalExtensions)),
    AccessMethod = extract(@"FTNTFGTui=([^;]+)", 1, AdditionalExtensions),
    ConfigPath = extract(@"FTNTFGTcfgpath=([^;]+)", 1, AdditionalExtensions),
    ConfigObject = extract(@"FTNTFGTcfgobj=([^;]+)", 1, AdditionalExtensions),
    ConfigAttributes = extract(@"FTNTFGTcfgattr=([^;]+)", 1, AdditionalExtensions)
| extend AdminSourceIP = coalesce(SourceIP, extract(@"(\d{1,3}(?:\.\d{1,3}){3})", 1, AccessMethod))
| where AdminUser !in (ApprovedAdmins)
| summarize
    StartTime = min(TimeGenerated),
    EndTime = max(TimeGenerated),
    ChangeCount = count(),
    ConfigPaths = make_set(ConfigPath, 25),
    ChangedObjects = make_set(ConfigObject, 25),
    ChangedAttributes = make_set(ConfigAttributes, 25),
    LogIds = make_set(LogId, 10),
    Messages = make_set(Message, 10)
    by FirewallName = DeviceName, AdminUser, AdminSourceIP, AccessMethod
| extend HighRiskChange = iff(tostring(ConfigPaths) has_any (HighRiskPaths), "Yes", "No")
| project StartTime, EndTime, FirewallName, AdminUser, AdminSourceIP, AccessMethod, ChangeCount, HighRiskChange, ConfigPaths, ChangedObjects, ChangedAttributes, LogIds, Messages

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: {{AdminUser}} made {{ChangeCount}} configuration change(s) on {{FirewallName}}. High-risk area changed: {{HighRiskChange}}.

properties.displayName: FW-008 Palo Alto - Configuration change or commit by administrator
properties.description: Detects configuration changes on Palo Alto Networks firewalls (PAN-OS CONFIG logs): add, delete, edit, set, move, rename, clone and commit commands. Each alert shows the administrator, the client used (Web or CLI), the configuration path and the result. Changes to security rules, admin accounts, NAT, VPN and log forwarding are flagged as high risk.
properties.query:
let lookback = 15m;
let HighRiskPaths = dynamic(["rulebase", "security", "nat", "mgt-config", "users", "admin", "log-settings", "network", "vpn", "ipsec", "global-protect", "zone"]);
let ApprovedAdmins = dynamic([]);   // optional: Panorama or automation accounts under change management
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor == "Palo Alto Networks" and DeviceProduct == "PAN-OS"
| where Activity =~ "CONFIG" or DeviceEventClassID =~ "CONFIG"
// Default PAN-OS CEF config format: act=$cmd duser=$admin destinationServiceName=$client msg=$path, result in the CEF header
| extend
    Command = DeviceAction,
    AdminUser = coalesce(DestinationUserName, SourceUserName),
    Client = DestinationServiceName,
    ConfigPath = Message,
    Result = iff(Activity =~ "CONFIG", DeviceEventClassID, Activity),
    BeforeChange = case(DeviceCustomString1Label has "Before", DeviceCustomString1, DeviceCustomString2Label has "Before", DeviceCustomString2, ""),
    AfterChange = case(DeviceCustomString1Label has "After", DeviceCustomString1, DeviceCustomString2Label has "After", DeviceCustomString2, "")
| where AdminUser !in (ApprovedAdmins)
| summarize
    StartTime = min(TimeGenerated),
    EndTime = max(TimeGenerated),
    ChangeCount = count(),
    Commands = make_set(Command, 20),
    ConfigPaths = make_set(ConfigPath, 25),
    Results = make_set(Result, 10),
    BeforeSample = make_set(BeforeChange, 5),
    AfterSample = make_set(AfterChange, 5)
    by FirewallName = DeviceName, AdminUser, AdminSourceIP = SourceIP, Client
| extend HighRiskChange = iff(tostring(ConfigPaths) has_any (HighRiskPaths), "Yes", "No")
| extend Committed = iff(tostring(Commands) has "commit", "Yes", "No")
| project StartTime, EndTime, FirewallName, AdminUser, AdminSourceIP, Client, ChangeCount, Commands, Committed, HighRiskChange, ConfigPaths, Results, BeforeSample, AfterSample

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: {{AdminUser}} ran {{ChangeCount}} configuration command(s) on {{FirewallName}}. High-risk area changed: {{HighRiskChange}}.

properties.displayName: FW-009 Firewall - Inbound connection allowed from a restricted country
properties.description: Detects inbound connections from public IPs located in a restricted country that the firewall allowed (FortiGate accept/close/timeout, Palo Alto allow). If your policy is to block these countries, any allowed session means a geo-blocking gap or a misconfigured rule. Country comes from the FortiGate srccountry field when present, otherwise from Sentinel's geo_info_from_ip_address().
properties.query:
let lookback = 1h;
// EXAMPLE list only. Replace with your organisation's or customer's restricted-country policy.
// Add every spelling your data uses (run the country check in docs/data-sources.md).
let RestrictedCountries = dynamic([
    "North Korea", "Korea, Democratic People's Republic of",
    "Iran", "Iran, Islamic Republic of",
    "Syria", "Syrian Arab Republic",
    "Cuba"
]);
// FortiGate logs allowed sessions as accept/close/timeout/*-rst; Palo Alto uses allow
let AllowedActions = dynamic(["accept", "allow", "close", "timeout", "server-rst", "client-rst"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor in ("Fortinet", "Palo Alto Networks")
| where isnotempty(SourceIP) and not(ipv4_is_private(SourceIP))
| where tolower(DeviceAction) in (AllowedActions)
| extend SourceCountry = coalesce(
    extract(@"FTNTFGTsrccountry=([^;]+)", 1, AdditionalExtensions),
    tostring(geo_info_from_ip_address(SourceIP).country))
| where SourceCountry in~ (RestrictedCountries)
| summarize
    StartTime = min(TimeGenerated),
    EndTime = max(TimeGenerated),
    SessionCount = count(),
    DestinationIPs = make_set(DestinationIP, 25),
    DestinationPorts = make_set(DestinationPort, 25),
    Actions = make_set(DeviceAction, 10),
    BytesSent = sum(SentBytes),
    BytesReceived = sum(ReceivedBytes),
    FirewallName = take_any(DeviceName)
    by SourceIP, SourceCountry, DeviceVendor
| project StartTime, EndTime, SourceIP, SourceCountry, SessionCount, DestinationIPs, DestinationPorts, Actions, BytesSent, BytesReceived, DeviceVendor, FirewallName

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: The firewall allowed {{SessionCount}} inbound session(s) from {{SourceIP}} in restricted country {{SourceCountry}}.

properties.displayName: FW-010 Firewall - Outbound connection allowed to a threat-intelligence IP
properties.description: Detects internal hosts making outbound connections to IPs that are active indicators in Microsoft Sentinel threat intelligence, where the firewall allowed the session. This can indicate malware calling its command-and-control server or data being sent to attacker infrastructure.
properties.query:
let dt_lookBack = 1h;
let ioc_lookBack = 14d;
let MinConfidence = 0;   // raise (for example to 50) if low-confidence indicators are noisy
// FortiGate logs allowed sessions as accept/close/timeout/*-rst; Palo Alto uses allow
let AllowedActions = dynamic(["accept", "allow", "close", "timeout", "server-rst", "client-rst"]);
let MaliciousIPs = ThreatIntelIndicators
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(ioc_lookBack)
    | where ObservableKey in ("ipv4-addr:value", "ipv6-addr:value", "network-traffic:src_ref.value", "network-traffic:dst_ref.value")
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by Id
    | where IsDeleted == false and (isnull(ValidUntil) or ValidUntil > now())
    | extend TI_Description = tostring(Data.description)
    | summarize arg_max(Confidence, TI_Description, Id) by TI_IP = ObservableValue
    | project TI_IP, TI_Confidence = Confidence, TI_Description, TI_IndicatorId = Id;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(dt_lookBack)
| where DeviceVendor in ("Fortinet", "Palo Alto Networks")
| where isnotempty(SourceIP) and isnotempty(DestinationIP)
| where ipv4_is_private(SourceIP) and not(ipv4_is_private(DestinationIP))
| where tolower(DeviceAction) in (AllowedActions)
| join kind=inner (MaliciousIPs | where TI_Confidence >= MinConfidence) on $left.DestinationIP == $right.TI_IP
| summarize
    StartTime = min(TimeGenerated),
    EndTime = max(TimeGenerated),
    SessionCount = count(),
    DestinationPorts = make_set(DestinationPort, 25),
    Applications = make_set(ApplicationProtocol, 10),
    BytesSent = sum(SentBytes),
    BytesReceived = sum(ReceivedBytes),
    FirewallName = take_any(DeviceName)
    by SourceIP, DestinationIP, TI_Confidence, TI_Description, TI_IndicatorId, DeviceVendor
| project StartTime, EndTime, SourceIP, DestinationIP, SessionCount, DestinationPorts, Applications, BytesSent, BytesReceived, TI_Confidence, TI_Description, TI_IndicatorId, DeviceVendor, FirewallName

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: Internal host {{SourceIP}} connected to malicious IP {{DestinationIP}}
alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: The firewall allowed {{SessionCount}} outbound session(s) from {{SourceIP}} to threat-intel IP {{DestinationIP}}.
